rule: Streamed responses render progressively. The streaming view IS the final view.
invariants: No flash or re-layout between stream-end and final rendered state.
Stream into a container with monotonically growing min-block-size to avoid jitter.
Token-by-token animation is decorative and respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Aria-live announcements are chunked to sentence or paragraph boundaries, not per-token.
Markdown / code block rendering handles mid-stream partial syntax gracefully (no angry-red errors during stream).

chunking.rationale: Humans read word-by-word; assistive tech cannot keep up with per-token updates.

cancellation.restore: Keep already-streamed content visible; mark response as 'canceled' rather than blank.

refusal: Buffer-to-completion server-side streaming that renders as one chunk.
Clearing the response area between stream-end and final render (causes flash).
